newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank raises main rate to 16.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank raises main rate to 16.50 pct.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Monday raised its central interest rate to 16.50 percent monthly from 15 percent.
"The BNB sets the main interest rate at 16.50 percent monthly, effective from Tuesday," the BNB said in a statement after a board meeting.
The BNB said on Friday it had decided to adopt a new approach towards setting the central interest rate (CIR) to enable commercial banks to link their interest rate policies to the market.

Under the decision the CIR would be set on the basis of the average weighted effective monthly yield of short-term T-bills auctioned daily by the finance ministry, and would be amended when significant changes in market conditions for short-term treasury paper occur, the BNB said.
Deepening financial crisis has prevented the BNB from cutting the CIR from its 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually, which has been in force since November 4.

The new main rate was calculated on the basis of 16.42 percent average weighted effective monthly yield of one-week T-bills and 18.80 percent yield of four week T-bills auctioned last week, the BNB said.

The finance ministry last week launched daily discount T-bill issues with maturities of one week and four weeks without setting par for them in advance in order to regulate excessive banks' liquidity.
Interbank depo rates rose on Monday following the BNB decision, dealers said.
Depo rate for deals of up to 14 days rose to 190 percent annually from 184-185 on Friday and one-month deals were struck at 225-228 percent, up from 186-188.
The rate for one- and two-day depos was unchanged at 180 percent annually while deals with terms of up to seven days were struck at 182-188 percent, up from 182-183 on Friday.
